newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: DOLLAR SEEN HIGHER AFTER PAUSE IN SINGAPORE.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR SEEN HIGHER AFTER PAUSE IN SINGAPORE.

text.p: The dollar was expected to resume its rise against the mark after some profit-taking and position squaring, Singapore dealers said on Friday.
"As long as we trade above 1.8570/75 in dollar/mark, we're in a consolidation pattern and set for a new upmove," a senior European bank dealer said.
He said dollar/yen was likely to struggle on the higher end but a renewed rally in dollar/mark would help to push it up.
"At the moment, people are locking in profits. Some are nervously squaring off longs but once we see new momentum, the dollar will head higher," he said.

Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke was quoted as saying the German central bank was watching forex developments very closely and would not move interest rates as long as there was no sign of inflation pressure.
Dealers said the market would scrutinise U.S. wholesale and consumer inflation data next week, for any indications of price pressure.
The U.S. Producer and Consumer Price Indices for July are due on August 13 and 14 respectively.
"It's important that the data are within expectations because if they overshoot, it will indicate a rate hike," the dealer said.
Support for the dollar could be dented if fears of a rate hike triggered outflows from U.S. stock and bond markets.
Some light short-covering was seen in sterling/mark after its overnight sell-off on indications the Bank of England's rate hike could be the last for some time.
Dealers said sterling/mark had slipped back after rising to the 2.9700 level earlier and the cross was likely to face selling pressure around 2.9730/40.

The Bank of England raised official interest rates by 25 basis points to 7.0 percent on Thursday but currency markets focused on the central bank's announcement that rates had now reached a level consistent with its inflation target.
